1.explanation:
1. packages/themes/src/g10.js and g100.js define all the theme color tokens for the g10 (light) and g100 (dark) themes, but neither file currently exports `$linkInverseHover` or `$linkInverseActive`. These files must be updated to import the correct blue and gray shades (e.g. `blue30`/`blue70` and `gray10`/`gray100`) and then export `linkInverseHover` and `linkInverseActive` with the values specified in the design.

2. packages/themes/src/white.js is the default (white) theme and likewise defines `inverseLink` but not the corresponding hover/active variants—if any other parts of the system fall back to the white theme in inverse contexts, they will also need those tokens.

3. packages/themes/src/tokens.js lists all of the token names that get emitted as CSS custom properties. It currently has `linkInverse` but lacks entries for `linkInverseHover` and `linkInverseActive`, so even after adding them in the theme files, the build system won’t generate the corresponding `--cds-link-hover-inverse` and `--cds-link-active-inverse` variables until they’re added here.
1.bug_scenario: The bug surfaces when using inverse-themed tooltips (dark backgrounds in light themes and light backgrounds in dark themes) with inline links. In the light theme (g10) tooltip, hovering over the "Learn more" link should use the `$link-inverse-hover` token (Blue 30, #a6c8ff), and activating (clicking) it should use `$link-inverse-active` (Gray 10, #f4f4f4). In the dark theme (g100) tooltip, the hover state should use the darker blue (`$link-inverse-hover`: Blue 70, #0043ce) and the active state should use `$link-inverse-active` (Gray 100, #161616). Currently those tokens are missing, so the CSS falls back to the default link tokens instead.
